text:
jamal: FYI noticed a weird token-count drift when converting HF tokenizer for the new model bring-up. 🤔
lena: how big is the drift?
jamal: on a small eval set, ~2-6% extra tokens on prompts that have trailing spaces or U+00A0 nonbreaking spaces.
maria: that sounds like a normalization mismatch. which normalizer did HF have?
jamal: HF tokenizer.json had "normalizer": { "type": "Sequence", "normalizers": [{"type":"NFKC"}] } but our Redwood pretokenizer pipeline applies NFC before byte-fallback.
lena: oh that's a subtle one — NFC vs NFKC changes composition of some characters (compatibility forms). can you paste an example?
jamal: sure. here's a failing case:

jamal: ```
# original string (visible spaces as ␣):
"hello world ␣"
# hf tokenizer tokens (using HF tokenizer.encode):
['▁hello', 'world', '▁']  # 3 tokens
# redwood local tokenize after conversion:
['▁hello', 'world', '▁', 'Ġ']  # 4 tokens (extra token from bytefallback/whitespace split)
```

alex: where is the extra token coming from? byte-fallback inserting explicit byte marker?
jamal: looks like when we NFC-normalize, a nonbreaking space becomes regular space in some cases, but HF's NFKC made a compatibility character fold into a single codepoint the tokenizer treats as prefix. our conversion script didn't port the HF normalizer pipeline; we only copied the vocabulary + merges.

maria: ok that explains the content-level diff. but why does that show up more under quantized runtime? shouldn't inference tokenization be identical?

jamal: quantized runtime uses a trimmed pretoken path for performance; we bypassed a small step that was re-normalizing compatibility forms to preserve perf. that step would've collapsed the compatibility whitespace into the expected token, avoiding an extra token.

lena: can we fix conversion script to copy HF normalizer block verbatim into the Redwood tokenizer config?

maria: yes, add both normalizer and pre_tokenizer sections. also double-check "byte_fallback" behavior. HF sometimes uses byte-level fallback to ensure roundtrip for unknown bytes. our implementation tags them differently (we add a dedicated token for \u{FFFD}-style fallbacks).

jamal: proposal: modify conversion pipeline to: 1) serialize HF normalizer config -> Redwood normalizer stage; 2) ensure pretokenizer whitespace handler matches (preserve prefix spaces semantics); 3) run small corpus diff tests (token counts + detokenize equality).

alex: +1. also add a quick unit test in onboarding CI that runs ~200 short prompts and fails if token-count drift > 1% or detokenize mismatch.

ci-bot: CI run started for branch jamal/tokenizer-fix — running tokenizer-regression-checker (200 prompts)…

qa: quick note: watch out for language-specific combining marks (Hebrew/Nepali) — NFC vs NFKC can reorder or decompose code points which changes grapheme boundaries and then tokenization alignment in chat templates.

maria: good catch. include mixed-script prompts in the diff test.

jamal: I'll open a PR with conversion fix + tests. attaching small repro script in the PR:

jamal: ```bash
python tests/tokenizer_repro.py \  --input examples/space_compat.txt \  --hf-tokenizer path/to/hf/tokenizer.json \  --redwood-conv path/to/converted/tokenizer.json
# script prints per-line: prompt | hf_tokens | rw_tokens | hf_detok == rw_detok
```

lena: can you also dump serialized normalizer configs in the PR so we can audit them?

jamal: will do. PR soon. TL;DR: root cause = HF used NFKC+specific pretokenizer whitespace semantics + byte-fallback behavior; our conversion missed the normalizer and subtly changed fallback token behavior, leading to extra tokens and small eval regressions, amplified in trimmed quantized runtime.
maria: thanks — this is exactly the sort of onboarding regression we should catch earlier. once PR lands run the full quantized eval suite. :thumbsup:
